A_general.open_code_note: No public source repository for the Akamai MCP Gateway at the input endpoint was found. Akamai's public Cloud MCP and Functions MCP repositories describe separate products and are not evidence of the deployed Gateway's implementation or tools.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.akamai.com/mcp is the URL configured by the Akamai Quick Deploy guide; it describes the same named MCP Gateway but differs from the input path /mcp/v1.
Akamai Cloud MCP (Linode) is a separate, public, read-only server: https://github.com/akamai-developers/akamai-cloud-mcp.
Akamai Functions MCP Server is a separate local server for Akamai Functions: https://github.com/akamai-developers/akamai-functions-mcp-server.
TrafficPeak documents a separate per-customer-host MCP endpoint at https://<your-trafficpeak-hostname>/mcp: https://techdocs.akamai.com/trafficpeak/docs/mcp-server.

contradictions: The input endpoint is https://mcp.akamai.com/mcp/v1, while Akamai's Quick Deploy configuration defaults to https://mcp.akamai.com/mcp and its example connection shows a token query parameter. The path and displayed token placement differ; the docs do not explain whether /mcp/v1 is an alias or separate tool surface.

The endpoint's WWW-Authenticate challenge identifies Bearer authentication, while the setup guide describes supplying an Akamai Gateway JWT and shows the client URL with a token query parameter. The relationship between these mechanisms is undocumented.
The pre-fetched OAuth discovery URLs returned HTTP 404; the official setup guide nevertheless requires a JWT. No OAuth metadata is exposed at the checked well-known paths.
observations_for_research: The documented client deployment is a Linode Compute instance configured to connect Claude to Akamai's separately managed Gateway; its compute plan is not stated as the Gateway's access price.
Public Akamai MCP repositories found in search describe distinct Cloud/Linode and Functions products; neither provides evidence about this hosted Gateway's implementation.
